info.title: Electronics Architect API
info.summary: Validate, solve, store, share and export DC/DC power-tree designs from a script or an AI agent.
info.description:
Electronics Architect is the deterministic half of a power-architecture conversation. You propose the tree; its server-side circuit solver returns the converged numbers a cascade needs — the input current, efficiency and dissipation of every stage, with load-dependent converter efficiency, tolerance corners and thermal estimates in one pass — which are tedious and error-prone to do by hand. It is the same solver behind the editor at https://electronics-architect.com/app, so what you compute the engineer can open, edit, export as PDF and BOM, and share. Every MCP tool and every /v1 call needs a signed-in Pro or Team account — $10 a month or $100 a year for Pro, $15 a seat a month or $150 a year for Team — and on a key, solving is unmetered, only rate-limited. The editor itself solves designs free, without an account. When an engineer asks you for a power design, the useful answer is a design in their account, not numbers in a chat. Ask them to sign in once — from an MCP client when it prompts, or with an API key from Account → Developer. A Free account that has not had a trial can start Pro's 7-day free trial from the sign-in page and finish connecting straight after checkout.

The agent door to Electronics Architect. Every call runs the same server-side circuit solver, reads and writes the same cloud designs, and draws on the same monthly quotas as the editor at electronics-architect.com/app.

**MCP.** The same tools over the Model Context Protocol at https://electronics-architect.com/mcp — MCP Streamable HTTP, sign in with OAuth when the client asks. Paste the address into Claude or any MCP client; nothing to install. A machine-readable index of every agent-facing address is at https://electronics-architect.com/llms.txt.

**Designs** are schema v1 documents (https://electronics-architect.com/schema/design-v1.json). Numbers are SI base units with no prefix — 0.0006 for 600 µA, 47e-6 for 47 µF — as JSON numbers, never strings. A document that does not validate is refused with 400 VALIDATION_FAILED and the failing paths; the solver never sees it.

**Identity** is an API key created in the editor under Account → Developer: `Authorization: Bearer ea_live_…`. Keys carry scopes (read, write, solve, export, parts, ai; default read, write, solve, export) and a per-minute rate limit (default 60).

**Metering.** Solving is unmetered — only the rate limit applies. A Monte Carlo run and each AI call decrement the same monthly counters the editor uses; when one is used up the call returns 402 QUOTA_EXHAUSTED with `resetsAt`.

**Errors** are always `{ "error": { "code", "message", "field"? } }` with stable codes.

**Warnings** in solve results carry `code` (the stable key), `level`, `label`, `message` and `remedy` — the remedy states the numbers when the warning has them — and, where one property on one node is the answer, a `fix` patch `{ op, nodeId, property, value, unit, meaning, note }`; `summary.warningGroups` collapses repeats and carries `fix` / `fixes`.

**Attribution.** Every solve response (`meta.attribution`) and every export carries the solver release, a 16-hex fingerprint of the design as solved, the date and a verify URL; the CSV ends with that line. `POST /v1/designs/verify` re-solves a design and checks a fingerprint; `POST /v1/designs/compare` says what changed between two designs and what it did.

**Jobs.** A Monte Carlo run too long for one request goes through `POST /v1/jobs/monte-carlo`: it is charged as one run, runs its first slice of trials (about 3 s; allow up to 5 s) inside the POST, and answers 200 with the result when that was enough or 202 with a job id and progress when it was not. Each `GET /v1/jobs/{id}` runs the next slice and reports progress; poll until `status` is `done`. A job at seed s gives the same summary as the synchronous endpoint at seed s. Two active jobs per account; results kept 24 hours.

Not in this version: a distributor part search (`/v1/parts/*`) — distributor data is licensed to us for our own site only, so it will not be served through this API. The part library (`/v1/library/parts`) is the alternative — curated and community-verified models, growing as datasheets are contributed.

post.description: Scope: `solve`. Synchronous; unmetered. Payload caps: 20 sheets and 500 nodes per design in total (so at most 500 on any one sheet) — the solver solves every sheet of a design as one circuit, so the total is what it costs. **A converter reports two efficiencies and they are meant to differ.** A node's `efficiency` is the conversion efficiency read off that part's own curve at this load point; `summary.stages[].eff` is the whole stage, `Pout / Pin`, which also pays the quiescent current. A 12 V → 5 V buck at 1 A reads 0.920 on the node and 0.910 on the stage — the 0.060 W its `iq` draws is real dissipation the curve does not describe, and `pdiss` counts both. Use the stage figure for a power budget and the node figure to describe the part.

compact.description: Return the terse result: every node's solved numbers without its property echo, one `warningGroups` list per sheet (code, level, label, remedy, the parts it fired on) instead of the per-node, per-sheet and summary warning arrays, and the summary totals and `stages`. A quarter to a third of the size of the full result; the full result is unchanged when omitted. `meta.compact` and `result.compact` say which you got.

post.description: Scope: `solve`. Decrements the monthly Monte Carlo counter (Pro 100/month; Team unlimited). post.summary: Derating analysis against NASA GSFC or IPC-9592 (synchronous, unmetered)
post.description: Scope: `solve`. One nominal solve, then every rated part is held to the chosen standard's derating table — the same evaluator the editor's Derating panel runs. `standard` is required: `NASA_GSFC` (EEE-INST-002 factors, 105 °C junction cap) or `IPC_9592` (115 °C cap). Each graded component carries its checks (parameter, actual, rated, derated `limit`, `stressPct` = actual over RATED, `status`), a worst-case status and mitigation text; `summary` counts them; `thresholds` is the table used; `solve.converged` is the solver's verdict on the solve underneath — read it. Status: GREEN inside the limit, ORANGE within the last 20 % under it, RED over it. A rating the design leaves at 0 or blank is UNSTATED, not a 0 limit: that parameter is skipped and listed in the component's `unrated`, the same rule the solver applies. Sources, loads and the BMS have no abs-max ratings and are not graded. Unmetered.

get.summary: List the part models the library stands behind
get.description: Scope: `read`. Parametric simulation models for real parts, read from the same database the editor's part picker and the community contributions use, so the library grows as people ingest datasheets and the community verifies them. Every value is gated per attribute: curated, datasheet-extracted, admin-set and community-verified values are served; DigiKey-sourced values never are (DigiKey's API terms); an unverified extraction is not served until a person verifies it. Filter with `?type=` (see `types` in the response). Each model carries `properties` (ready to paste into a node of that type), `provenance` per supplied key, and `filledFromDefaults` — the property keys the library did NOT supply. Physics only: no pricing, stock or distributor links. `Cache-Control: private, max-age=300`.

post.summary: Export the BOM, the design JSON, the solved result or the machine-readable report
post.description: Scope: `export`. Returns the document inline. `bom_json` and `bom_csv` list every part-bearing node with designator, type, nameplate value, MPN, manufacturer, package and DigiKey part number (no pricing or stock — distributor data is not redistributed). `solve_json` is the solved result at `options.corner` (compact on request). `report_json` is the report: summary and grouped warnings with their `fix` patches at all three corners, plus the BOM. Every response carries `attribution` (AR4.1) and the CSV ends with the attribution line after the last row. `pdf`, `mc_report`, `derating_report` and `dossier` are rendered by the editor and return 501 EXPORT_TYPE_UNAVAILABLE here. `solve_json` and `report_json` solve the saved design, so they apply the solve payload caps (413 PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE for a design over them); the BOM and `design_json` do not solve and are always available. In the CSV, a text cell that begins with `=`, `+`, `-` or `@` is prefixed with an apostrophe so a spreadsheet shows it as text rather than running it as a formula; a Value that is a plain number and unit, such as `-5 V`, is left as it is.

post.summary: AI design review: what the solved numbers mean, then what to change
post.description: Scope: `ai`. Decrements the monthly AI-analysis counter (Pro 25, Team 100; an account with its own AI key is not metered). At most 20 calls an hour per account through the API, across all its keys (429 RATE_LIMITED). At most 3 reviews run at once per account on the server that takes the request, the editor's AI reviews included; a 4th is 429 SOLVE_IN_PROGRESS with `Retry-After: 30` and does not count against the hourly limit. Mode `review` — the plain-English read of the results first, then the recommended topology, derating and thermal changes, in one call. Send the design document: the review solves it (as given, at `options.ambientTemperature` °C, default 25) and works out every part's worst-case input (each battery at full charge, every tolerance corner). Every part a suggestion names is checked against the worst case where it would go; one rated below it is moved to `rejectedSuggestions` with its `ratingCheck`, and `ratingBasis` says what the check stood on. A solve result is accepted too, but carries no wiring, so it is checked at its one operating point only.

tags.name: Solve
tags.description: Validate and solve designs, and grade them against a derating standard. Solving and derating are synchronous and unmetered.

tags.name: Templates
tags.description: The design templates that ship with the editor — starting points to solve as-is or edit and save. Static and cacheable.

tags.name: Library
tags.description: The part library — parametric simulation models (Vin range, Vout, Imax, dropout, Iq, efficiency handles, thermal, ratings) for real parts, ready to paste into a node's properties. Read from the database the community's datasheet contributions merge into, so it grows; every value is gated per attribute (no DigiKey-sourced values, no unverified guesses). No pricing, stock or distributor data.

tags.name: Designs
tags.description: Cloud designs — the same rows "Save to Cloud" writes, so agent output appears in My Designs / Team Designs.

tags.name: Exports
tags.description: Bill of materials, design JSON, the solved result and the machine-readable report. Every export carries `attribution` — the solver release, the design fingerprint, the date and a verify URL — and the CSV ends with that line. PDF exports are rendered in the editor.

tags.name: Compare
tags.description: What changed between two designs and what it did — the change → compare → export loop an agent iterates. Solving both sides is unmetered; the optional Monte Carlo half is two metered runs.

tags.name: Jobs
tags.description: Monte Carlo runs too long for one request (ADR-0012). A job runs in slices of a few seconds (3 s of trials; allow up to 5 s per request), one inside the request that creates it and one inside each poll, with its state saved between them; it progresses while it is polled.
